items.title: Section: Craving in Every Feeling, Every Time, Every Object

items.zh: 當知遍起復有三種。一者、位遍。依一切受差別轉故。謂由五門。喜和合故、喜不離故、喜不合故、喜乖離故、常隨自身而藏愛故。二者、時遍。謂緣去來今三世境故。三者、境遍。謂緣現法、後法內身而起，亦緣已得、未得境界而起。
items.en: It should be known that pervasive arising is further of three kinds. First, pervasive across feeling-states, operating according to the differences among all feelings. This occurs through five gates: delighting in union, delighting in non-separation, delighting in non-union, delighting in separation, and always cherishing and clinging to oneself. Second, pervasive across time, referring to objects of the past, future, and present. Third, pervasive across objects, arising with respect to the present body and the future body, and arising also with respect to objects already obtained and not yet obtained.

items.title: Section: Squid Ink in Clear Water — Why Freedom Means Freeing the Mind, Not Avoiding the World

items.zh: 問：何故唯說離貪瞋癡，心得離欲，不說離色受等煩惱事耶？答：由離於此，亦離彼故。又諸煩惱性染污故。又即由此多過患故。所以者何？若於其事起諸過患，當知皆是煩惱所作。是諸過患，如前蘊善巧中觀察不善所有過患。又可避故。所以者何？於諸事中，一切煩惱皆可避脫，非一切事。
items.en: Question: why is it said that freeing the mind from greed, hatred, and delusion alone constitutes freedom from desire, rather than freeing oneself from form, feeling, and the other afflicted matters? Answer: because freeing oneself from these also frees one from those. Also, because the very nature of these afflictions is defiled. Also, precisely because of this, they carry many faults. Why is this so? Whatever faults arise in any matter should be known as entirely the affliction's own doing. These faults are as already explained when observing the faults of the unwholesome under the skilful understanding of the aggregates. Also, because they can be avoided. Why is this so? Among all matters, every affliction can be avoided and escaped, but not every matter itself.

items.title: Section: Better to Fall From Hell Than Never Leave the Peak of Existence

items.zh: 又由修習不淨觀等諸世俗道，雖厭其事，入離欲地，然離欲地煩惱隨逐，煩惱於心未得離欲。由此道理，唯離煩惱心善離欲，非離其事。於此處所餘決擇文，更不復現。問：何因緣故，於諸經中，從餘煩惱簡取我、我所見、我慢執、著、隨眠，說為染污煩惱品耶？答：由三因故。一、向邪行故，謂我、我所見二種故。所以者何？依止身見以為根本，便能生起六十二見；依託此故，於非解脫計為解脫，而起邪行。二、背正行故。謂我慢、執著二種。所以者何？依止我慢、執著故，於此正法毘柰耶中所有善友，所謂諸佛及佛弟子真善丈夫，不往請問云何為善，云何不善。設彼來問，亦不如實顯發自己。三、退勝位故。謂隨眠一種。所以者何？雖到有頂，下地隨眠所隨逐故，復還退墮。
items.en: Also, one who cultivates mundane paths such as the contemplation of impurity, though wearied of the matter at hand and thereby entering the ground of freedom from desire, still has affliction following along even in that ground, the mind not yet freed from desire. For this reason, only freeing the mind from affliction is rightly called freedom from desire, not freeing oneself from the matter itself. On this point, the remaining deciding-discernment text does not appear again. Question: for what reason do the sutras, apart from other afflictions, single out self-view, self-belonging-view, self-conceit, attachment, and latent tendency, calling these the defiled class of affliction? Answer: for three reasons. First, tending towards wrong conduct, referring to self-view and self-belonging-view. Why so? Taking embodied-selfhood-view as the root, the sixty-two views arise; relying on this, what is not liberation is computed as liberation, and wrong conduct arises. Second, turning away from right conduct, referring to self-conceit and attachment. Why so? Relying on self-conceit and attachment, one does not go to the good friends within this correctly taught doctrine and discipline, namely the buddhas and the true, good persons among the Buddha's disciples, to ask what is wholesome and what is not. Even if asked by another, one does not honestly reveal oneself. Third, regressing from an exalted position, referring to latent tendency alone. Why so? Though one reaches the peak of existence, followed still by the latent tendency of the lower grounds, one falls back down again.

items.title: Section: Four Things Only the Buddha's Teaching Has

items.zh: 復有差別。謂通達所知，於滅作證，有二種法極為障礙。一、邪行因緣，二、苦生因緣。邪行因緣者，謂六十二見。因此執故，於諸有情由身語意起諸邪行。苦生因緣者，謂不斷隨眠故。又此二業有二因緣。邪行因緣因緣者，謂計我、我所薩迦耶見。苦生因緣因緣者，謂初後兩位不起正行。由我慢故，初不聞正法；由增上慢故，後不修正行。復有差別。謂於善說法毘柰耶中，有四種法為最、為上、勝極、勝妙、不共外道。何等為四？一者、於諦簡擇；二者、於己同梵行所，修可樂法；三者、於異論所不生憎嫉；四、於清淨品能不退失。於惡說法毘柰耶中，有四種法，於此四法極為障礙。一、計我、我所薩迦耶見，二、我慢，三、妄執諦取，四、不斷隨眠。由此因緣，雖到有頂，必還墮落。又有二執。一、根、境執，謂執我、我所。二、展轉有情執，謂我慢，計我為勝等。
items.en: There is a further difference. In the well-taught doctrine and discipline, there are four things that are foremost, supreme, utterly excellent, and wondrous, shared by no outside teaching. What are the four? First, discerning the truths. Second, cultivating agreeable practice among one's own fellow practitioners in spiritual life. Third, not harbouring resentment or envy towards differing doctrines. Fourth, not regressing from purity. In wrongly taught outside doctrine and discipline, there are four things that greatly obstruct these four. First, self-view and self-belonging-view. Second, self-conceit. Third, falsely grasping and clinging to a view of the truths. Fourth, failing to sever latent tendency. For this reason, though one reaches the peak of existence, one must fall back down again. There are also two kinds of attachment. First, attachment to faculty and object, meaning attachment to self and self-belonging. Second, attachment arising in mutual comparison among beings, meaning self-conceit, computing oneself as superior and so forth.

items.zh: 問：自有貪愛為眾苦因，何故餘處世尊復說欲為苦因？答：以是現法苦因緣故。所以者何？若於有情有欲、有貪、或有親昵，彼若變異，便生憂惱等苦。問：何故五蓋說名為龜？答：五支相似故，能障修習如理作意故。

items.title: Section: A Mother Camel, Congealed Blood, and Meat on the Butcher's Block

items.zh: 問：何緣故忿說名母駝？答：似彼性故，由惡語者，於他言詞不能堪忍增上力故，能障得彼教授教誡。問：何故慳、嫉說名凝血？答：由於虛薄無味利養而現行故，能障可愛樂法故。問：何故諸欲說名屠机上肉？答：繫屬主宰無定實故，能障無間修善法故。問：何故無明說名浪耆？答：似彼性故，障聞智故。問：何緣故疑說名岐路？答：似彼性故，障思智故。問：何故我慢說名輪圍？答：似彼性故，障修智故。問：更有所餘能發惡行無量煩惱，何故簡取貪瞋癡，立不善根？答：發業因緣略有三種。謂愛味因緣故，損他因緣故，執著建立邪法因緣故。此貪瞋癡於上因緣，如應配釋。
items.en: Question: why is wrath called a mother camel? Answer: because its nature resembles that creature, since one of harsh speech, by the very power of being unable to bear another's correction, is obstructed from receiving instruction and admonishment. Question: why are stinginess and envy called congealed blood? Answer: because they manifest through attachment to thin, flavourless gain, and obstruct agreeable practice. Question: why are desired objects called meat on the butcher's block? Answer: because they belong to no fixed master, and obstruct the uninterrupted cultivation of wholesome dharmas. Question: why is ignorance called a wolf? Answer: because its nature resembles that creature, obstructing the wisdom of hearing. Question: why is doubt called a forked road? Answer: because its nature resembles that image, obstructing the wisdom of reflection. Question: why is self-conceit called an encircling mountain range? Answer: because its nature resembles that image, obstructing the wisdom of cultivation. Question: there are countless other afflictions capable of generating unwholesome conduct — why are greed, hatred, and delusion alone singled out and established as the unwholesome roots? Answer: in brief, there are three conditions generating karmic action: the condition of relishing with craving, the condition of wishing to harm another, and the condition of clinging to and establishing wrong dharma. Greed, hatred, and delusion should be correlated with these conditions accordingly.

items.title: Section: A Closing Verse, and Fascicle Fifty-Eight's Own Natural Resting Point

items.zh: 中嗢拕南曰：欲、愛、離欲、計我等、欲、龜駝母等、及貪瞋等。
items.en: The verse placed at the chapter's midpoint says: desire and craving, freedom from desire; computing a self, and desire as a cause of suffering; the tortoise, the mother camel, and their companions; and greed, hatred, and the rest.

blocks.text: The fascicle ends with similes and a sharp warning: even the highest worldly absorption is not freedom.
Master Cháng Bǎi: in any feeling, craving appears in a different form; it takes aggregates, beings, and worlds of all three times.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the aggregates are ripened results and will appear; objects keep arising, but one can refrain from affliction, and that is freedom.
Master Cháng Bǎi: absorption only presses seeds down; however high one rises within the three realms, one can still fall. Only severing seeds is a well-freed mind.

subs.head: What only the Buddha's teaching has

blocks.text: Master Cháng Bǎi: through the four noble truths beings penetrate reality; where others think differently, they feel no hatred. Outsiders cling to the six faculties as self and the six objects as theirs.

Master Cháng Bǎi: a person of harsh speech cannot bear admonition; wavering about the Dharma is like standing at a fork in the road; pride is like encircling mountains, hard to cross. (Untranslated, 0626c03: why desire is called a cause of present suffering: what we love changes and brings grief; and why the five hindrances are compared to a tortoise: they are five like its limbs, and block proper attention.)
Master Cháng Bǎi: relishing produces greed, harming produces hatred, and clinging to wrong doctrine produces delusion.
A complete anatomy of affliction: its kinds, its roots, how it binds, and how it is cut. Its central lesson: the objects are not the problem; the craving is.

quiz.q: What are craving's three kinds of pervasive arising?
options: across the desire, form, and formless realms, feeling, time, and object being included within those and not listed separately in the treatise
across body, speech, and mind
across vision, cultivation, and no more training
across feeling-states, across time, across objects
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: in any feeling, pain, pleasure, sorrow, joy, or equanimity, craving appears in a different form; it takes aggregates, beings, and worlds of the three times; it rises on the present and future body and on things gained and not gained. The English is accurate.

quiz.q: Why speak of freedom from greed, hatred, and delusion, not from form and feeling?
options: faults are affliction's work; affliction can be avoided, aggregates being results; rightly, objects arise without affliction
form and feeling are themselves unwholesome but too many to leave at once
form and feeling do not exist
form and feeling are pure
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: greed, hatred, and delusion can be avoided, while the aggregates are ripened results that will appear; objects keep arising, but one can refrain from affliction, and that is the correct way. The English "the other afflicted matters" is close to 煩惱事.

quiz.q: Why is worldly detachment through impurity contemplation not true freedom?
options: because impurity contemplation is an outsiders' method, true freedom being simply to leave all women and wealth, the mind then being naturally free
worldly paths cannot reach absorption
it only presses down manifestation, and absorption can regress; only severing seeds is true freedom
the detached ground has no seeds
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: absorption only presses down seeds so they do not manifest, and so one can fall from it; only departing from affliction and severing its seeds is called the mind being well freed from desire. This matches the earlier analysis of worldly severing at §45.

quiz.q: Why do the sūtras single out self-views, conceit and attachment, and latent tendency?
options: wrong conduct: latency; right conduct: self-views; regression: conceit
tending to wrong conduct; turning from right conduct; regressing from an exalted position
all three tend to wrong conduct
all three cause regression
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: holding what is not the path of liberation to be liberating produces wrong conduct of the three doors; conceit and attachment keep beings from learning the Dharma. Latent tendency brings regression. The English follows this.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain falling back though reaching the peak of existence?
options: gods of the peak willingly descend at others' request out of compassion, not falling, latency playing no real role in the lecture's view
the peak has no limit of life
only the desire realm falls
with seeds unsevered, however high one goes one falls, even from the peak
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: affliction seeds make beings fall back, however high they have cultivated within the three realms; though one reaches the peak of the three realms, one will still fall to the lower realms. The English matches the Chinese here.

quiz.q: What four things are unique to the well-taught doctrine and discipline?
options: ethics, absorption, wisdom, and liberation, the roots of the Dharma that others lack
discerning the truths; agreeable practice among companions; no envy of other views; not regressing from purity
the four mindfulnesses
the four immeasurables
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: through discerning the four noble truths, the causes and results of the world and beyond, beings penetrate reality; where others think differently, they feel no hatred or envy; purity does not regress because seeds are severed. A good passage for interfaith teaching.

quiz.q: The English has "There is a further difference." Against the lecture's outline, which meaning is this, and what is missing?
options: the first; §53's three reasons do not count, the exposition beginning here, nothing being missing, the lecture treating this as the start
the fourth; the tortoise simile is missing
the third; the second, on wrong conduct and the arising of suffering obstructing realisation, is wholly missing
the second; nothing is missing
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi calls this the third explanation of why self-views and the like are the defiled class. The second, beginning "there are two things that obstruct realising the knowable and cessation," is absent from both Chinese and English here, so "a further difference" reads as the second.

quiz.q: What are the two attachments, and how do outsiders cling?
options: to faculty and object: self and mine; among beings: conceit, reckoning oneself superior
self-attachment and dharma-attachment, the vehicles differing
views and precepts
greed and hatred
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: outsiders cling to the inner six faculties of a living being as self and the outer six objects as belonging to self. The second attachment arises in comparing oneself with others. The English is a clear rendering here.

quiz.q: What are wrath, stinginess and envy, and desires likened to, and what do they obstruct?
options: mother camel: continuous cultivation, being slow; congealed blood: instruction; butcher's meat: agreeable practice, meat delighting people
all three obstruct the wisdom of hearing
mother camel: instruction; congealed blood: agreeable practice; butcher's meat: continuous cultivation
all three obstruct the wisdom of cultivation
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a person of harsh speech has no patience at all when admonished; attached to thin and flavourless gain, they cannot bear others' gain. Thus each simile matches one obstruction. The English "belong to no fixed master" captures 無定實.

quiz.q: What do the forked road and the encircling range stand for, and which wisdom does each block?
options: doubt, a forked road, blocks reflection; conceit, an uncrossable range, blocks cultivation
conceit, the road, blocks hearing; doubt, the range, blocks reflection
greed the road; hatred the range
both block hearing
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: wavering about the Dharma is like standing at a forked road, blocking the wisdom of reflection; conceit is like the encircling mountains, hard to cross, blocking the wisdom of cultivation. Ignorance blocks the wisdom of hearing, so the three wisdoms are matched in order.

quiz.q: The English has "a wolf" for 狼者. How does the lecture, citing Shentai, read this, and what caution applies?
options: one reading only, the steppe wolf, fiercest of devourers, so that "wolf" is the only correct rendering, needing no further note on sources
狼者 is a personal name to be transliterated
狼者 means a shepherd
the lecture has two readings, Shentai's being a weasel; "wolf" does not fit that, and the rendering is undecided
quiz.why: The lecture gives both, noting that 狼 may be a weasel, citing Shentai through the Commentary, whose image of a tail blocking a snake fits the idea of obstructing hearing. "Wolf" fits only the first reading. The question records the disagreement rather than deciding it, so a translator's note is the safest fix.

quiz.q: Why are greed, hatred, and delusion the unwholesome roots, and how do the three conditions match?
options: relishing to delusion; harming to greed; wrong dharma to hatred
relishing to greed; harming another to hatred; establishing wrong dharma to delusion
all three match greed
all three match delusion
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the condition of relishing produces greed, that of harming others hatred, and that of clinging to and setting up wrong doctrine delusion. The treatise leaves the matching to the reader with 如應配釋, rendered "accordingly" in the English.
